intro: TRANSACT actively contributes to the international research community through workshops, conference presentations, invited lectures, and the organization of scientific panels. These activities foster collaboration, disseminate research findings, and strengthen an international network dedicated to Freedom of Information (FOI), transparency, and democratic governance.

items.title: How Public Institutions Create Value for Society in Complex Governance Systems: Bridging Politics and Public Administration
lines: Giovanni Esposito was invited as one of five international emerging scholars to present his research agenda on public administration, transparency, and comparative governance. The roundtable brought together researchers from Europe, North America, and Asia to discuss new directions for international collaborative research in public administration.

The presentation showcased the broader research programme underpinning TRANSACT, highlighting its practice-based approach to Freedom of Information implementation and its combination of randomized field experiments and computational social science. The event also provided the opportunity to strengthen collaborations with South Korean scholars and to advance preparations for the South Korean field experiment, developed in partnership with Inha University as part of the TRANSACT comparative research programme.

Participants: Ana-Maria Dimand (Florida State University), Andrew Sullivan (University of Central Florida), Ning Liu (City University of Hong Kong), Wenchi Wei (Tsinghua University), and Giovanni Esposito (Université libre de Bruxelles).
Organizers: Donwe Choi (Hanyang University) and Jinsol Park (Inha University).

items.title: Transparency in Action – International Perspectives from Experimental Research on Freedom of Information Laws
lines: TRANSACT organized a two-day international workshop bringing together leading scholars and practitioners working on Freedom of Information laws and transparency governance. The workshop combined research presentations, roundtables with civil society organizations, and collaborative sessions dedicated to designing comparative field experiments in Belgium, Romania, Switzerland, South Africa, and Uganda. It laid the foundations for the international research network that now supports the TRANSACT project.
